decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be selected for this candidate?
decision_log.choice: O1 — Sequential staged pipeline with explicit council role pods.
decision_log.rationale: Branch B01B requires maximum conservatism and risk aversion. O1 provides the simplest reproducible execution model, unambiguous checkpoint boundaries, and the easiest model for high HITL scrutiny. The linear audit trail directly addresses CNS1, CNS3, and CNS6. The trade-off of slower wall-clock time is explicitly acceptable per the branch risk posture.
alternatives_considered: O2 — Task-parallel fan-out/fan-in: rejected due to higher orchestration complexity, merge conflict risks, and more complex checkpoint/resume model that conflicts with the conservative posture.
O3 — Checkpoint-driven micro-cycle with partial freeze: rejected because partial freezes add downstream complexity and the big-bang strategy requires a single holistic freeze.
O4 — Monolithic council: rejected due to low modularity, risk of weakening role separation internally, and reduced auditability of internal stage transitions.
what_would_change_this_decision: If wall-clock execution time becomes a hard constraint requiring parallelism.
If the target repositories have many independent tasks that would benefit significantly from parallel lanes.
If partial-freeze capability becomes a requirement for long-horizon budget management.

evidence_pointers.note: Branch B01 specifies O1, big_bang, high HITL

decision_log.question: What milestone strategy should be used?
decision_log.choice: Big-bang: single linear pipeline with one final freeze event.
decision_log.rationale: The branch specification mandates big-bang milestone strategy. All requirements and acceptance tests must be satisfied in one comprehensive freeze bundle. This prevents incremental drift and ensures holistic review, aligning with the extremely risk-averse posture and high HITL strictness.
alternatives_considered: Incremental milestones with partial freezes (O3-style): rejected per branch specification; adds downstream complexity for consumers handling incomplete bundles.
Parallel milestone tracks: rejected; incompatible with O1 sequential pipeline and big-bang strategy.
what_would_change_this_decision: If long-horizon execution consistently exceeds token/time budgets, requiring partial-freeze checkpoints.
If downstream consumers require incremental delivery of implementation artifacts.

decision_log.question: How should HITL strictness be configured?
decision_log.choice: High HITL strictness: every escalation trigger requires human approval before proceeding.
decision_log.rationale: The branch risk posture is extremely risk-averse, prioritizing auditability and predictability. High HITL involvement mitigates K1 (scope expansion), K2 (audit spine breakage), K5 (policy bypass), and K10 (role separation failure) through mandatory manual scrutiny at every escalation point.
alternatives_considered: Medium HITL: auto-approve low-severity escalations. Rejected per branch specification.
Low HITL: orchestrator handles most decisions autonomously. Rejected; incompatible with risk-averse posture.
what_would_change_this_decision: If execution speed becomes critical and the risk profile of the target repositories is well-understood.
If automated validators achieve sufficient coverage to reduce the need for human review at lower-severity escalation points.

decision_log.question: How should repair loops be bounded and selection be deterministic?
decision_log.choice: Orchestrator enforces per-stage iteration caps and per-repair-cycle operation caps. When multiple candidate patches pass validation, the smallest passing repair is selected using deterministic tie-breakers: fewest operations → fewest bytes changed → first-generated.
decision_log.rationale: R15 mandates deterministic smallest-passing-repair selection. Bounded repair loops prevent infinite iteration and align with the conservative posture. The tie-breaker order is explicit and auditable.
alternatives_considered: Allow unbounded repair iterations: rejected; risks exhausting budgets and stalling the pipeline.
Use quality-weighted scoring for repair selection: rejected for this branch; adds complexity and subjectivity incompatible with deterministic posture (K21 notes this as a future consideration).
what_would_change_this_decision: If the simplistic selection logic consistently produces sub-optimal patches (K21), secondary deterministic scoring signals could be added.

evidence_pointers.note: K21: smallest passing repair simplicity risk

decision_log.question: How should tool permissions be enforced across stages?
decision_log.choice: Deny-by-default tool permission matrix per stage, with sandboxed execution. Network is denied by default across all stages. Repo writes are allowed only via patch_apply in PatchApply and IntegrateAndValidate stages. Reviewers have no write permissions. All denials are logged in the audit spine.
decision_log.rationale: CNS1 requires orchestrator-sole authority over tool permissions. The deny-by-default posture with sandboxed tooling (per branch governance_posture.tooling_level) minimizes blast radius. High HITL strictness means any permission expansion requires human approval.
alternatives_considered: Permissive defaults with post-hoc auditing: rejected; incompatible with sandboxed tooling level and high HITL strictness.
what_would_change_this_decision: If specific stages require network access (e.g., dependency resolution), explicit allowlisting with HITL approval would be added per K15 mitigation.

supplemental_evaluations.notes: All 23 acceptance tests (AT1–AT23) are mapped to milestone exit criteria. AT1–AT3 are covered by M1 (Intake). AT4–AT6 are covered across M1–M7 (stage sequence and handoffs). AT7 is covered by M7 (Freeze Bundle). AT8 is covered by M1 and M7. AT9 is covered by M3. AT10–AT11 are covered by M5 and M6. AT20 is covered by secrets scanning at every milestone. AT21 is covered by M7 (freeze gates). AT22 is covered by M5 and M6 (role separation). AT23 is covered by M4 (flaky failure handling).

supplemental_evaluations.title: Risk Coverage Assessment
supplemental_evaluations.notes: All 22 risks (K1–K22) are addressed by the candidate design. K1 (scope expansion) is mitigated by work plan semantic validation (M2), reviewer findings-only enforcement (M5), and HITL on ChangeRequests. K2 (audit spine) is mitigated by immutable run_manifest and append-only event_log enforced from M1 through M7. K3 (evidence standard) is mitigated by RFC 6901 enforcement at every milestone. K4 (security vulnerability) is mitigated by security scanning in M4 with HITL on critical findings. K5 (repo protection bypass) is mitigated by forbidden-path enforcement in M3 and M5. K6 (flaky tests) is mitigated by deterministic retry policy in M4. K7 (secrets leakage) is mitigated by secrets scanning at every milestone. K8 (workspace integrity) is mitigated by workspace_index validation at every milestone. K9 (context pack overflow) is mitigated by bounded context pack compilation by orchestrator. K10 (role separation) is mitigated by multi-vendor routing and output-type allowlists in M5 and M6. K11 (JSON Patch misuse) is mitigated by op cap and schema revalidation in M5. K12 (merge conflicts) is low risk in O1 sequential pipeline since there is no parallel execution. K13 (AT trace mismatch) is mitigated by AT# mapping in M4. K14 (release artifact safety) is mitigated by freeze gates in M7. K15 (supply chain) is mitigated by network-deny default. K16 (over-broad refactors) is mitigated by patchset size caps in M3. K17 (checkpoint/resume) is mitigated by stage_handoff at every milestone. K18 (decision integrity) is mitigated by evidence-pointer requirements in M6. K19 (tool permissions) is mitigated by deny-by-default matrix. K20 (upstream ambiguity) is mitigated by intake validation in M1. K21 (repair selection) is mitigated by deterministic tie-breakers. K22 (workspace growth) is mitigated by retention/compaction policies in workspace_context.json.

supplemental_evaluations.title: Big-Bang Strategy Trade-off Analysis
supplemental_evaluations.notes: The big-bang milestone strategy maximizes holistic review quality and prevents incremental drift, but introduces a key risk: if the pipeline fails late (e.g., at Judge or Freeze), all prior work must be re-evaluated. In O1's sequential model, this is partially mitigated by stage_handoff artifacts at every boundary enabling deterministic resume from the last passing checkpoint. However, there is no partial-freeze escape valve—if budgets are exhausted before Freeze, the run produces no frozen output. This is an accepted trade-off per the branch's risk posture, which prioritizes correctness over partial delivery.

glossary.definition: A CouncilOS subsystem that consumes a frozen planning output (plan_package_final.json) and produces audited, reproducible repository changes and release artifacts under orchestrator-controlled policies and validators.

The canonical, typed/versioned set of JSON artifacts emitted at freeze, including run manifest, event log, work plan, patchsets, repo snapshot, test/quality/trace/review/release artifacts, decision record, and required workspace artifacts (workspace_index, context_packs, stage_handoffs).

A tool-accessible, versioned and auditable storage area treated as an extension of the artifact system, containing canonical JSON artifacts and explicitly non-canonical notes/summaries, governed by permissions, retention, and checkpoint/resume handoffs.

An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer object {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note} referencing a versioned JSON artifact location; used as the sole standard for traceability across decisions, findings, and state representations.

A required JSON artifact emitted at each checkpoint boundary capturing resumable state: objectives, completed work, pending blockers, next actions, and pointers into canonical artifacts (work plan, patchsets, validation outputs).

A canonical artifact proposed when plan semantics would need to change; requires explicit decisioning and policy-triggered escalation (HITL and/or reroute upstream) before any semantic deviation is allowed.
Deterministic code component with sole authority over routing, budgets, iteration limits, termination, checkpoint/resume, tool permissions, selection logic, and validator enforcement.
A bounded, deterministically-compiled set of workspace artifacts provided to a role at a stage, selected by explicit rules and cited via evidence pointers.
A JSON artifact embedding code diffs with deterministic apply order for repo modifications; used as the sole mechanism for code repair/changes in the workflow.
A code-owned deterministic gate that checks artifact integrity/completeness and quality criteria to allow stage transitions or freeze.
